name: GTranslate Visual Addon
author: tuwebmaster

sections.description:
GTranslate Visual Addon helps you fix wrong, literal, or missing GTranslate translations directly from the frontend. Click any visible text, add your preferred translation, and override the automatic output for visitors using that language.

This plugin acts as a bridge and enhancement for the GTranslate service. You must have the core GTranslate plugin installed and active for this to work. By using this plugin, you are also bound by the GTranslate Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Use it for targeted fixes when GTranslate misses or mistranslates:

  • WooCommerce buttons and checkout labels.
  • Elementor text widgets.
  • Contact forms.
  • Custom theme strings.
  • Headings, buttons, and calls to action.

If GTranslate missed it, you can translate it manually. If GTranslate translated it poorly, you can fix it with a visual translation editor.

How it works

  1. Make sure GTranslate is installed, active, and visible on your site.
  2. Log in as an administrator and navigate to the frontend of your website.
  3. Use GTranslate to switch to the language you want to customize.
  4. Select the specific translated text visually from the page.
  5. Type your custom translation.
  6. Save it. Your custom text will override the automatic translation whenever visitors switch to that language.

Scope of the Free Version

This free version is built for targeted fixes: up to 10 visual text overrides for 1 target language.

It is useful for small websites, landing pages, WooCommerce labels, form text, headings, buttons, and other critical strings where automatic translation needs a manual correction.

Discover the Pro Version

Need to correct hundreds of strings across multiple languages?

The Pro Version is a separate plugin that offers additional features for GTranslate power users:

  • Unlimited Visual Elements translated without restrictions.
  • All Languages Supported simultaneously.
  • CSV Import/Export: Manage thousands of translations in Excel and upload them in seconds.
  • SEO Title & Meta Translation: Translate your <title> and <meta description> tags to rank every language on Google.

Discover GTranslate Visual Addon Pro here

External services

GTranslate Visual Addon includes optional anonymous telemetry for compatibility and product-improvement decisions. It is disabled by default. No telemetry request occurs unless an administrator explicitly enables it and saves the preference.

When enabled, one request per week is sent to https://tuwebmaster.com.ar/wp-json/tuwebmaster/v1/telemetry containing a random installation identifier, WordPress/PHP/plugin versions, locale, translation and configured-language counts, and yes/no compatibility flags for GTranslate, GTranslate Visual Addon Pro, Elementor, and WooCommerce.

Telemetry never includes the site URL, administrator or visitor details, translation text, container selectors, license data, or browser user-agent strings. Tu WebMaster stores a one-way hash of the random identifier and retains records for up to 180 days. Source IP is not stored in the telemetry database; standard hosting security logs may process it under the privacy policy.

Disabling telemetry stops future requests and sends a deletion request for that installation record. Uninstalling the plugin does the same when telemetry was enabled.

sections.installation:
1. Go to your WordPress Dashboard -> Plugins -> Add New.
  2. Search for GTranslate and ensure it is installed and active.
  3. Upload the gtranslate-visual-addon folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install it directly via the WordPress Plugin Directory.
  4. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  5. Go to the frontend while logged in as an administrator, switch to the target language with GTranslate, and start selecting visual elements to customize.
sections.faq:
Do I need GTranslate installed for this to work?

Yes. This plugin acts as an addon for GTranslate. GTranslate handles language switching, and this plugin lets you correct selected text manually.

Can I manually fix wrong GTranslate translations?

Yes. Log in as an administrator, switch to the target language with GTranslate on the frontend, then select visible translated text and save a manual override.

Can I edit a translation that GTranslate already did?

Yes. If GTranslate’s automatic translation is too literal or incorrect, click that text with the visual selector and type your custom translation. Your version will take priority.

Can I use it with WooCommerce or Elementor?

Yes for visible frontend text. It is useful for targeted fixes such as buttons, labels, headings, form text, and checkout wording.

What is included in the free version?

The free version supports up to 10 visual text overrides for 1 target language. It is designed for targeted translation fixes.

How can I get unlimited translations, multiple languages, and CSV Support?

These professional features are available in the separate GTranslate Visual Addon Pro plugin. Click here to learn more about the Pro Version.
sections.changelog:
3.5.2

  • Added a dismiss control to hide the floating Translation Mode interface until the page is refreshed.
  • Prevented private translation controls from loading in WordPress administration and visual builder editing contexts.
  • Kept the public translation engine active inside builder previews while excluding Elementor, Divi, and other common editor interfaces.

3.5.1

  • Added an administrator-only floating Translation Mode control with or without the WordPress admin bar.
  • Added a centered, dismissible quick-start guide using the administration brand palette.
  • Explained how to finish editing and identify existing custom translations when returning to Translation Mode.
  • Added a curved guide line pointing to the floating button and kept the button clickable above the guide overlay.
  • Completed an extensive security and compatibility review with successful results.

3.5.0

  • Fixed frontend re-editing so an existing custom translation can be updated without deleting it in the dashboard.
  • Declared GTranslate as a required plugin using the native WordPress plugin dependency system.
  • Added disabled-by-default anonymous telemetry with explicit administrator consent, weekly delivery, and remote deletion on opt-out.
  • Added a responsive administration sidebar for Tu WebMaster services, support, privacy information, and telemetry preference.
  • Documented external service behavior, collected compatibility fields, retention, and privacy safeguards.

3.4.4

  • Redesigned the contextual review invitation with a softer, modern interface aligned with the plugin’s brand palette.
  • Added a brief, human message explaining how reviews support continued updates and improvements.
  • Updated the WordPress admin header and review invitation to use the current GTranslate Visual Addon logo.
  • Normalized release file names and line endings for WordPress.org packaging and coding standards.
  • Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.0 and GTranslate 3.1.1.
  • Passed the official WordPress Plugin Check with AI analysis enabled and no errors or warnings across General, Plugin Repository, Security, Performance, and Accessibility checks.

3.4.3

  • Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.0.
  • Added a new reviews module.
  • Performed routine maintenance and compatibility updates.
  • Improved plugin stability through additional testing.
  • Synchronized the internal plugin version.

3.4.2

  • Updated product URLs for the Pro version.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release on the WordPress Repository.
  • Added visual frontend string capturer.
  • Integrated base GTranslate bridging system.
  • Added feature to override automatic translations.
  • Implemented Lite restrictions (10 strings, 1 language).
